items.title: John "Knocky" Parker Interview, 1963-08-28
items.q: I always liked Russell. Russell Robinson's playing in 1920, aggravating Papa came out and I remember that's one of the tunes

ctx.x: You want to go into more detail on the early music?

We used to have itinerant musicians who'd come through there and from the beginning I'd learned how to play by copying the notes going down on the player piano. Put a roll in and see the notes going down and then make the same notes go down in the same combinations. Children have keenly, keen sensitivities and can watch things going on and can absorb more being children somehow than we as adults can. Innovations of immortality and all that. And as a child you can see keenly little patterns going down, patterns of…
that I used to like mainly. What generally were the kind of roles that you had around the house?
